D.t: Amy Klobuchar leads by 14.9 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 415,242 votes; a one point swing is about 13,944 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +7.7 and D +21.8. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +9.5. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +17.4; your worst is co/efficient (R) at D +5.9. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 348,334 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 139,566 votes; Dakota, a projected net 54,467 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +4.7, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +1.1, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, D +1.9, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +9.6, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Amy Klobuchar runs furthest behind in Stearns, Sherburne, Wright. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 53 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.76 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 61 to 36, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Amy Klobuchar: Immigration voters 26 to 71, Small counties 38 to 59, Voters who can afford daily costs 47 to 50. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$3.5M cash against $618K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $6.2M helping Lisa Demuth and $1.3M helping Amy Klobuchar.

The polls page average is D +9.5. Your best recent poll is co/efficient (R) at D +5.9; your worst is New York Times/Siena at D +17.4. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Stearns, a projected net 18,760 votes; Wright, a projected net 17,538 votes; Sherburne, a projected net 14,699 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +4.7, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +1.1, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, D +1.9, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +9.6, 1.1% of the vote.

R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lisa Demuth runs furthest behind in St. Louis, Ramsey, Hennepin. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 44 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 42 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.76 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 36 to 61, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Lisa Demuth: Black voters 16 to 82, Health care and Social Security voters 22 to 75, Asian and other voters 23 to 74. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$618K cash against $3.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
